our_takes.our-take: The DBS Chromo Card does the category-picking for you: each month it identifies your top two eligible local spend categories out of Dining, Travel, Shopping, Transport, Entertainment and Wellness, and applies up to 5% cashback to them, with 1% on other local spend. You can also toggle the whole card to miles mode instead and earn 1.3 miles per S$1 on eligible local spend, uncapped and with no minimum. The annual fee is waived for the first five years, and there's no foreign transaction fee on overseas or foreign-currency spend. Worth a look if you're in your twenties, spend mostly in SGD, and want a card that adjusts to your spending instead of asking you to predict it.
our_takes.good-for:
Cardholders in their 20s who'd rather not pre-select cashback categories — Chromo applies bonus cashback to your top two local spend categories automatically each month.
People whose spending shifts month to month, since the bonus follows where you actually spent rather than a choice locked in earlier.
Anyone who wants the option to toggle between cashback and miles monthly on the same card, without a new application.
our_takes.things-to-note:
You must be 21–29 at the point of application. You can keep the card past 30, but from the fourth month after your 30th birthday the rewards drop to a flat 1.7% cashback or 1.3 miles per S$1.
Bonus cashback needs a minimum S$500 local spend in the calendar month. Miss it and everything that month earns the 1% base rate.
Total cashback is capped at S$150 per calendar month, covering base and bonus combined.
Foreign currency spend pays no cashback and no miles. It counts towards the S$500 minimum, but the 0% FX fee is the only benefit you get on overseas spend.
